summary: Makoto Nagai was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Tokyo from around 1904 to 1907. He later held academic posts at the University of Tokyo (~1913–1942) and Toyo University (~1942–1957).

Makoto Nagamura is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who attended Azabu Junior and Senior High School. He served as a professor at Japan Women's University from around 1991 to 2017.

Makoto Yoshimura is a specialist in Buddhist studies and Sinology who completed doctoral coursework at Waseda University between 1993 and 1998. Around 2005, he served as an assistant professor at Komazawa University.

Malcolm David Eckel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his doctorate at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served on the Harvard faculty (~1980–1990, ~1998–2000) and at Boston University (~1990–2021).

Mamoru Tonami was a scholar of Sinology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Kyoto University from 1956 to 1965. He later held a post at Otani University from around 2000 to 2008.
Manabendu Banerjee is an Indologist who served as Co-ordinator for DSA Sanskrit at Jadavpur University, attested in 2003. He has also held the post of Secretary at the Asiatic Society.

Manfred Mayrhofer was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Graz under Wilhelm Brandenstein. He held posts at Würzburg (~1958–1963), Saarland (~1963–1966), Vienna (~1966–1988), and the Austrian Academy of Sciences (~1982–1985).
Manfred Steger is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy who studied at Rutgers University and under Robert Aitken. He held a post at RMIT University from around 2004 to 2013.
Manfred Taube was a Tibetologist who studied under Friedrich Weller between around 1948 and 1957. In 1991, he held a professorship in Central Asian studies at Leipzig University.

Manshi Kiyozawa was a Buddhist studies scholar and philosopher who studied at Toyo University and under Ernest Fenollosa at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Toyo University (~1890–1896) and Otani University (~1901–1903).
Manudeva was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under the traditional teachers Bālakṛṣṇa Pāyaguṇḍa and Bāla Śarman Pāyaguṇḍe.

Marc Aurel Stein was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied in Vienna, Leipzig, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. His posts included Oriental College Lahore, University of the Punjab, and the Archaeological Survey of India.
Marc Tiefenauer is an Indologist who completed his PhD at the University of Lausanne by 2016 under the supervision of Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Nahid Rouzbeh.

Marc-Henri Deroche is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He pursued his studies under doctoral supervisor Matthew T. Kapstein as well as teachers Fernand Meyer, Samten Gyaltsen Karmay, Katsumi Mimaki, Heather Stoddard, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Marcel Granet was a Sinologist who studied at the École Normale Supérieure and under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at the EPHE, INALCO, the Institut des Hautes Études Chinoises, and the Collège de France.

Marcel Mauss was a scholar of religious studies who studied at the University of Bordeaux from around 1890 to 1895. He held academic posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1901–1940) and the Collège de France (1931–1942).

Marcelle Lalou was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi, Jacques Bacot, Paul Pelliot, and Jean Przyluski. She held a post at EPHE from around 1926 to 1962.

Marco Walther is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his doctorate at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under Franz-Karl Ehrhard, attested in 2017, and also studied under Khenpo Dondrub Namgyal.

Marcus Bingenheimer is a Buddhist studies scholar and Sinologist who earned his doctorate at Würzburg under Norbert Klaes. He held posts at Dharma Drum institutions, Chung-Hwa Institute, and Temple University.

Marek Mejor is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held a junior research fellowship at Wolfson College, Oxford, from 1981 to 1982 and served as a professor at the University of Warsaw, attested from 2000 to 2010.
